title: NumCache: KV Cache Compression and Retrieval for Financial Document QA

problem.claim: Financial question answering over SEC filings requires reasoning over extremely long, numerically dense documents and across documents.

gap.claim: Existing long-context, compression, retrieval, and cache-based approaches do not adequately preserve fine-grained numerical values or ensure that caches are well-formed and query-relevant.

contributions.claim: NumCache compresses SEC filings into KV caches initialized from numerically dense regions and trained directly on financial question-answer pairs.
A contrastive retriever aligns questions with cache representations to improve retrieval performance.
NumCache is evaluated on Fin-RATE tasks spanning single-filing reasoning, cross-firm comparison, and longitudinal trend analysis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: NumCache achieves up to 4× context compression with 41.4% accuracy versus 44.8% for uncompressed Qwen3-4B on single-filing reasoning, and provides a 6.4× inference speedup.
The contrastive retriever achieves 68.3% Recall@1 on single-filing retrieval, compared with 29.7% for the strongest text-based baseline.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are increasingly used to interpret SEC filings in financial applications.
Financial QA over SEC filings is difficult because of document length, numerical density, and cross-document reasoning requirements.
Existing methods struggle with long-context degradation, numerical fidelity, and construction of query-relevant caches.
NumCache builds number-focused KV caches and trains a contrastive retriever over their representations.
The authors report compression, accuracy, speed, and retrieval results on Fin-RATE.

source_observation.claim: The approach initializes caches from numerically dense regions and trains them on financial QA tasks.

interpretation.claim: Domain-specific cache construction may help preserve information that generic semantic compression loses.

application.claim: For numerical long-document QA, prioritize representations and retrieval objectives that preserve values and units.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond SEC-filing financial QA.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the cache architecture, training procedure, or data splits.
The abstract does not report results for all Fin-RATE task categories.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
